title: Expansion Sprint Plan — 740-Item Backlog to Executable Content Programs

immediate.description: High-priority, foundation-building items that unlock subsequent work
categories: Pilot cohort (50 items) — pipeline validation across all 6 domains
Analyze items for high-gap domains: Section C (60), Section D (50), Section A (50)

near_term.description: Scale-up items once pipeline is validated and velocity is established
categories: Evaluate items across all 6 domains (100 items)
Analyze items for remaining domains: Section B (40), Section E (25), Section F (15)
Part 2 Financial Decision Making items (150 items)
Very Difficult standalone MCQ items (50 items)

sprint_1.name: Foundation & Pipeline Validation
sprint_1.description: Execute S836 50-item pilot cohort. Validate quality-first pipeline end-to-end. Establish velocity baselines.
deliverables: 50 Certified items with zero defect-class violations
Pipeline velocity metrics (time per item, rejection rate, certification rate)
Updated S836 pipeline spec with lessons learned
Proof that quality-first approach produces zero DL-008/DL-026/DL-013 on first pass
risks: Pipeline may reveal unforeseen authoring bottlenecks
Evaluate items may require multiple revision passes
Very Difficult items may exceed time estimates
sprint_1.mitigation: Start with Apply/Analyze items first; defer Evaluate to batch 2 after pipeline is proven on mid-tier items

sprint_2.name: Analyze Scale-Up
sprint_2.description: Scale the validated pipeline. Target the largest cognitive gap: 160 net-new Analyze items across all 6 domains.

batches.focus: Section D: Cost Analysis + Decision Making

deliverables: 160 Certified items, all passing quality-first pipeline gates
Analyze inventory grows from 10 to 150 items (0.4% → 5.9% of pool)
First Evaluate inventory established: 20 items (0.8% of pool)
Domain coverage: Analyze items distributed across all 6 sections
risks: Volume pressure may erode quality discipline
Distractor engineering for 160 items is labor-intensive
sprint_2.mitigation: Gate-based: any item failing Stage 5 Evidence Review is rejected, not patched. Velocity takes priority over throughput.

sprint_3.name: Evaluate & Advanced Content
sprint_3.description: First dedicated Evaluate sprint. Also includes advanced case-based items and Very Difficult standalone items.
deliverables: Very Difficult inventory: 0 → 80 items (0% → 3.1% of pool)
risks: Evaluate item authoring is cognitively demanding — higher rejection rate expected
Case-based items require exhibit creation which adds complexity
sprint_3.mitigation: Allow 50% higher time budget for Evaluate items. Pilot case-based items in small batches before scaling.

sprint_4.name: Part 2 Expansion Launch
sprint_4.description: First Part 2 content sprint. Builds Part 2 Foundation, blended with remaining Part 1 higher-order items.
deliverables: 1,080 total new items across all 4 sprints
risks: Part 2 blueprint requires new domain expertise
sprint_4.mitigation: Apply all S836 pipeline gates without exception. Each Part 2 item must pass same 6-stage pipeline as Part 1 items.

certified_yield.description: ~15% Stage 5 rejection rate; rejected items recycled in next sprint

defect_rate_target.description: Pipeline designed for zero defect-class violations per item; any violation = rejected

remediation_load.description: Near-zero expected — quality-first pipeline eliminates template-origin defects; only author errors remain

risk_factors.pipeline_velocity: LOW — pipeline is new, actual times may exceed estimates by 30-50%
risk_factors.evaluate_complexity: MEDIUM — Evaluate items require novel distractor engineering (trade-off distractors vs single-error distractors)
risk_factors.part_2_expertise: MEDIUM — Part 2 content may require additional blueprint study before authoring
risk_factors.cognitive_fatigue: MEDIUM — Long authoring sessions risk quality erosion at higher cognitive levels
risk_factors.governance_compliance: LOW — Pipeline gates + governance guard provide redundant safety net

post_sprint_2.notes: Analyze items near 6.1% of pool; first substantial higher-order inventory

post_sprint_3.notes: Evaluate reaches 4.4% of pool; Very Difficult reaches 3.7%

post_sprint_4.notes: Part 2 pilot established; higher-order items now 26% of pool (vs. 4.8% at start)

governance.defect_tracking: Any new defect discovered during authoring must be logged to DEFECT_LIBRARY.md per AGENTS.md §12
